title: Finite split-step source, beta, volume and shape uniformity stress audit
question: Does the finite split-step recurrence pass persist under declared source, beta, volume and shape changes with the same C=J=1 constants and both term orders?
method: Retain the EXP-001156 exact onsite-plus-all-bond split product, oscillator dimension 3, delta=1/18, six steps, both real-time signs and both A/A* contexts.
Evaluate the canonical target/square/2x3 graphs at volumes 2, 4 and 6 for the baseline source pair (0,1), then separately evaluate beta=1/2 and beta=2 at volume 6.
Evaluate shifted source pairs (1,2) at volume 4 and (3,4) at volume 6, and path-shaped stress graphs at volumes 4 and 6.
Cache only exact matrix factors common to a declared case, compare all rows to the same C=J=1 recurrence, reproduce them in a non-importing lane, and cross-check rational fixtures in Lean R327.
finding: Primary 559/559, independent 558/558, integrated 155/155, and Lean R327 compile PASS. The persisted lanes contain 2464 commutator-length rows and 2112 recurrence rows each. No violation occurs in any case, order or context. Primary maximum residuals by case are baseline_canonical_beta1_source01=1.64553048496507e-14, canonical_beta_half_v6=1.662813170245e-14, canonical_beta_two_v6=1.65309083175331e-14, canonical_shifted_source=1.83980565155742e-14, and path_shape_source01=1.48584855450973e-14, all below the declared 1e-9 recurrence tolerance.
decision_reason: The finite split recurrence is stable across the declared source, beta, volume and shape stress cases with both term orders. This is stronger finite applicability evidence than EXP-001156, but it remains a sampled matrix audit and does not provide the analytic uniform estimate required for common-alpha promotion.
boundary: Finite oscillator-dimension-3 matrices, the declared five cases, beta in {1/2,1,2}, source pairs listed in the manifest, six steps, two product orders, both signs and both adjoint contexts. The path graph is a stress geometry and is not claimed as the canonical Q3 lattice. No cutoff removal, arbitrary-shape exhaustion, exact CCR common core, thermodynamic dynamics, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion follows.

adversarial_review.check: Baseline volume growth, two beta changes, shifted sources and path-shape stress are all explicit manifest cases; no unlisted case is generalized.
Both onsite-first and reverse term orders are tested for every case.
Initial q/p commutator lengths outside each declared source pair are checked against the finite tolerance.
Each beta case rebuilds the normalized Gibbs state from the same finite Hamiltonian; no beta-independent state is assumed.
The largest residual is a sampled finite value; it is not promoted to a supremum or analytic constant.
The second lane reconstructs oscillator, graph, split Hamiltonian, Gibbs state and seminorm without importing primary code.
R327 proves only rational fixtures and scope; it does not formalize matrix exponentials or uniformity.
No common alpha, thermodynamic limit, OS/KMS/GNS or gap follows from finite stress agreement.

qft_interface.closed: Finite split-step recurrence rows remain valid across the declared source, beta, volume and shape stress cases.
qft_interface.open: Analytic source/beta/volume/cutoff uniformity, arbitrary shapes and exhaustion, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

next_action: Replace the finite stress sampling with an analytic state-weighted or energy-graph bound uniform in source, beta and volume; then test product/core density and exhaustion before common-alpha promotion.
no_overclaim: This is finite stress evidence only. It does not prove a uniform recurrence theorem, a thermodynamic limit or any downstream QFT or TECT sector theorem.
